about: Facts the certificate must keep. scripts/check_fidelity.py checks each one against facts.json, so that a change to Certificate/Facts.lean cannot quietly lose them. They answer Astra's outside review (docs/reports/outside-review-01.md), which asked for these regressions by name; brief 0005, stage 1k. Each names an entry by its ref and a field of it (Certificate/FIELDS.md), and asks that the list `includes` some names, `excludes` others, or holds exactly `count.is` names beginning with `count.prefix`; `equals` compares the field with a value. A field that is an object, as `inherited` is, is read by its keys, and a field the entry lacks fails. `why` is shown when one fails.

expectations.why: The porism's own entry pins every assumption of its proof by the argument of Euclid's reductio from the given centre: 51 tacit rules, with centre_unique excluded. It neither calls III.1 nor uses exists_centre.
III.1's certificate now also carries exists_centre through its construction, for D within by III.2's argument: 56 tacit rules, still without centre_unique.
A porism's entry names its proposition.
A proposition lists its porism, so that it is not complete until the porism is proved.

III.2's own Lean does not call Circle 2 (Argon's second review; #65). Since Circle 2 is now a theorem, excluding its name from own_axioms no longer checks for such a call; the separate axioms pin excludes its underlying Circle 3.

No lemma that III.2 calls uses Circle 2 (#65). Since Circle 2 is now a theorem, excluding its name from inherited no longer checks for such a use; the separate axioms pin excludes its underlying Circle 3.
I.5's own Lean never calls Postulate 3: like Euclid's proof, it draws no circle (#65).

Postulate 3 reaches I.5's proof through Book Zero's exists_between_nearer, which keeps a point taken at random near enough with a circle; a lemma's axioms are inherited, not the proof's own (Argon's second review; #65).

III.2 does not rest on Circle 3: its own Lean calls neither Circle 3 nor the theorem Circle 2, and III.1, which it cites, shows its middle point within the circle by III.2's own argument (#60). Circle 2's retired name is also kept out of the axiom list.
III.1 shows the middle point of its chord within the circle by I.5, I.16 and I.19, as III.2 does, and does not rest on Circle 3 (#60). Circle 2's retired name is also kept out of the axiom list.

II.14 puts E within the circle by Definition I.15 and the order of the points (InsideCircle.of_between_centre), and does not rest on Circle 3 (#60). Circle 2's retired name is also kept out of the axiom list.
None of the eight retired names may appear as an axiom in III.1's certificate. Each now names a theorem with the same type; a proof that uses it lists its underlying axioms instead.
